A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EAPO research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved from the main text into appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical reasoning evaluations, policy/expert scaling experiments, parallelism ablations and training dynamics in Tables 1–3 and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds non-math evaluations, consultation-schedule comparisons, expert-quality experiments and a Qwen3-8B policy evaluation.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains learnable expert consultation, parallel queries, the same reward and objective, reciprocal consultation annealing and independent test-time reasoning. Alternative schedules and model configurations are evaluated as ablations; they do not replace the default method.

E1.justification: v2 adds HumanEval, HLE, GPQA, MMLU, EvalPlus, HotpotQA and SimpleQA evaluations, extending coverage into coding, scientific reasoning and question answering. It also tests erroneous and uninformative expert-input scenarios. DAPO-Math training and the three original mathematical benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: The principal comparison methods in Table 1 remain unchanged. Appendix H adds a budget-matched fixed-rate consultation baseline and slower/faster annealing alternatives directly compared with default EAPO in Table 9, providing a focused extension of the comparator set.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce budget-matched schedule controls, selection of three erroneous expert trajectories from 32 samples, and replacement of guidance with fixed uninformative text. Additional configurations include Llama-8B experts, stronger offline experts and a Qwen3-8B policy. The original mathematical evaluation protocol and core training hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds expert-pool homogeneity ablations, consultation-schedule sensitivity and budget controls, offline noisy-guidance and stronger-expert tests, and another policy-family evaluation. These substantially extend analysis of complementarity, consultation timing and dependence on model choice. Original training-dynamics analyses and case studies are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions describe 32 sampled answers and the same variance across per-problem mean scores. v2 adds no training-seed counts, independent-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Additional variance entries extend the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–2 and Figure 3 retain their results. New results include non-math averages of 49.25 for EAPO versus 47.15 for self-exploratory RL, and Qwen3-8B averages of 49.98 versus 45.44. Schedule and expert-quality results are also added. Section 3.2 changes the stated distillation comparison from 20.83% to 24.80% without changing the underlying scores.

T1.justification: Trajectory probabilities, rewards, optimization objectives and evaluation-statistic definitions remain substantively unchanged. v2 clarifies history indexing and symbols but adds no theoretical result, proof or substantive mathematical derivation. Alternative schedule formulas specify experimental settings.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion expand the central performance claim from mathematical reasoning to robust cross-domain transfer after math-only training. On-demand consultation, assistance internalization and the approximately five-point mathematical advantage remain the original core claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning complementary expert capabilities, consultation timing beyond total call budget, transfer beyond mathematics and applicability across policy families. Appendix D discusses coding failures when expert capabilities are poorly matched. Appendix E additionally claims bounded noise sensitivity, although its described offline workflow tests do not directly establish robustness of EAPO training.

D1.justification: v2 documents exact alternative consultation rates, erroneous-trajectory selection and fallback rules, and an example uninformative guidance message. It also explicitly states a shared interaction budget for the existing parallelism comparison. Original hyperparameter tables, prompts, model/data access information and vLLM configuration remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for the seven new benchmarks and two Chen et al. works on long-horizon agents. The existing positioning against expert-guided distillation, hierarchical RL and self/social learning remains largely intact. The Policy Distillation publication-year update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: v2 polishes several introduction and explanatory paragraphs, clarifies notation, revises headings and moves consultation dynamics and offline collaboration discussion into appendices B–C. The main section sequence and most existing method, related-work and implementation prose remain recognizable; the revision primarily expands scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 adds seven result tables, groups Table 1 by method category and adds an average column to the relocated offline comparison. It also adjusts diagram typography and Figure 3's legend, enlarges the response-length plot, and moves the consultation-rate figure into Appendix B. These substantially expand and reorganize the displays.

improvement.justification: v1 leaves cross-task generalization as future work and lacks a control separating consultation timing from total consultation budget. v2 addresses these important gaps with math-only transfer evaluations, a budget-matched schedule comparison and another policy-family evaluation (Tables 4, 9 and 11). These substantially strengthen empirical support. Sparse non-math evaluation details and Appendix E's overextension of offline robustness evidence limit some new claims but do not outweigh the gains.
